Certification Tracking Software for NDT: ASNT and ISO 9712

How certification tracking software enforces ASNT SNT-TC-1A and ISO 9712 compliance automatically.

By Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III · July 24, 2026

Certification tracking software for NDT centrally manages technician qualifications under ASNT SNT-TC-1A written practices or ISO 9712 third-party certification, recording method, level, exam and renewal dates, and automatically restricting report sign-off and job assignment to technicians whose certification is current and matches the required scope.

Why Certification Tracking Cannot Stay in a Spreadsheet

Every NDT company eventually hits the same failure mode: a spreadsheet tracking technician certifications gets updated inconsistently, someone forgets to flag an upcoming renewal, and a Level II technician ends up signing a report under a certification that lapsed three weeks earlier. In isolation this looks like an administrative slip. In an audit, or worse, in litigation following a failed asset, it becomes a documented compliance failure that undermines the validity of every report that technician issued during the gap. Certification tracking software exists specifically to remove the human memory dependency from this process.

SNT-TC-1A Written Practice vs. ISO 9712: What Software Needs to Support

SNT-TC-1A is an employer-based qualification system: the employing company writes its own practice defining training, experience, and examination requirements for each level, and internally certifies technicians against that practice. ISO 9712 is a third-party certification scheme, technicians are certified by an independent, accredited certification body rather than their employer. Companies operating internationally or serving clients who require ISO 9712 often need to track both systems simultaneously, sometimes for the same technician holding both credentials for different clients or jurisdictions. Certification tracking software needs to model both systems accurately, including the different renewal cycles and recertification requirements each imposes, rather than forcing everything into a single generic certification field.

What Certification Tracking Software Actually Does

At a functional level, a proper certification tracking module maintains a record per technician covering method (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD, Phased Array), level (I, II, III), certifying body or internal written practice reference, initial certification date, expiration date, and supporting documentation such as exam results and vision test dates. It surfaces this data at the point where it matters most, when a technician is being assigned to a job or when a report is being signed, rather than as a passive record someone has to remember to check separately.

Enforcing Sign-Off Rules Automatically

The difference between certification tracking as a passive database and certification tracking as an active compliance control is enforcement. Software that simply displays a technician's certification status still relies on a human catching the problem. Software that blocks a Level I technician from independently signing a final report, or prevents assignment of a technician whose certification for a specific method has expired, removes that dependency entirely. This single enforcement rule addresses one of the most common findings during client vendor qualification audits and third-party quality reviews.

Renewal Alerts and Expiry Management

Certification renewal typically requires lead time, scheduling a recertification exam, completing required continuing experience hours, or renewing vision testing, none of which can happen instantly the week a certification lapses. Software should generate renewal alerts at 90, 60, and 30 days ahead of expiry, escalating to management if no action has been logged, so recertification is planned proactively rather than reactively discovered when a technician is already scheduled onto a job requiring that credential.

Vision Testing and Experience Hour Tracking

Both SNT-TC-1A and ISO 9712 require periodic vision acuity and color perception testing as a condition of maintaining certification, along with, for many levels, documented experience hours in the applicable method. Certification tracking software should capture these as structured fields tied to each technician's record, not as separate paperwork disconnected from the certification itself, since an auditor reviewing a technician's qualification file expects to see vision testing and experience documentation alongside the certification record, not filed separately.

Client Vendor Qualification and Audit Readiness

Major oil and gas, petrochemical, and power generation clients run vendor qualification programs that require inspection companies to produce current certification records for every technician assigned to their sites, often on short notice. Companies with certification data centralized in software can generate this documentation in minutes. Companies relying on manual file organization frequently scramble to assemble it, sometimes discovering gaps only during the audit itself. Fast, accurate certification documentation is increasingly a competitive differentiator in vendor qualification, not just a compliance checkbox.

Connecting Certification to Scheduling and Work Orders

Certification tracking delivers its full value when connected directly to project and work order management, so a technician cannot be assigned to a job requiring API 510, 570, or 653 inspection scope unless their certification for the relevant method and level is current at the moment of scheduling, not just at the time the roster was last reviewed. This closes the gap between a certification record technically existing in the system and that record actually being checked before it matters.

Certification Tracking as Part of Full NDT ERP

Certification tracking delivers the most value as one connected module inside a broader NDT ERP platform, alongside calibration management, project scheduling, and reporting, rather than as an isolated point solution. When certification, calibration, and scheduling data all live in the same system, the cross-checks that prevent compliance gaps happen automatically as part of normal operations instead of requiring a separate manual review step. Companies evaluating this as part of a broader platform decision should review the full picture of ERP built for NDT inspection companies, which folds certification tracking into the same system as reporting, calibration, and invoicing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: What is the difference between SNT-TC-1A and ISO 9712 certification?

A: SNT-TC-1A is an employer-based system where the company writes its own practice and certifies technicians internally. ISO 9712 is third-party certification issued by an independent, accredited certifying body. Companies serving international clients often need to track both simultaneously.

Q2: Can certification tracking software prevent an expired certification from being used?

A: Yes, when properly implemented, the software actively blocks scheduling or report sign-off for a technician whose certification has expired or does not match the required method and level, rather than just displaying a status that relies on someone checking it manually.

Q3: How far in advance should certification renewal alerts trigger?

A: Best practice is staged alerts at 90, 60, and 30 days before expiry, giving enough lead time to schedule recertification exams and complete required experience hours or vision testing before the credential actually lapses.

Q4: Does certification tracking software help with client vendor qualification audits?

A: Yes, centralized certification records let companies generate current, accurate documentation for client vendor qualification programs in minutes rather than manually assembling files, which reduces both audit stress and the risk of discovering compliance gaps during the review itself.

Q5: Should certification tracking be a standalone tool or part of ERP?

A: It delivers the most value connected to scheduling, calibration, and reporting inside a full NDT ERP platform, since the automatic cross-checks that prevent compliance gaps require certification data to interact directly with work order assignment, not sit isolated in a separate system.
